title: Exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (GAR (stock)) (template 3)
heading: Exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (GAR (stock)) (template 3)
start_phrase: RBI’s assets with exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities at year-end 2024 amounted to € 1,072 million and are used in the calculation of the GAR (CapEx).
summary:
- Scope and data limitations: Due to limited structured data—especially for use‑of‑proceeds transactions—RBI could not include its full relevant portfolio in the GAR assessment. RBI expects taxonomy-eligible and -aligned shares to rise as client disclosures improve. NACE codes are assigned based on the counterparty’s main business using public registries and an external data provider.

- Taxonomy eligibility/alignment view: A CapEx-based breakdown shows total assets split into covered vs. excluded assets and into not eligible/not assessed, eligible, and aligned buckets. GAR is calculated on covered assets (denominator), not total assets.

- GAR (stock) results: Year-end 2024 exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities totaled €1,072 million for inclusion in the GAR (CapEx). The overall GAR (CapEx) was 0.81%.

- Retail treatment and MS safeguards: All retail exposures relevant to the EU Taxonomy were analyzed for both CapEx and turnover GAR. Following the Platform on Sustainable Finance guidance, minimum social safeguards were not applied to retail exposures. Taxonomy-aligned retail activities amounted to €41 million, contributing 0.03 percentage points to the 0.81% GAR.

- Retail methodology details: House purchase loans were assessed against NZEB thresholds and “top 15%” national building stock primary energy demand for activity 7.7, using transparent real data per EU Commission FAQs. Estimates (e.g., by year of construction) were only in voluntary disclosure. Due to data gaps, building renovation and car loans were generally treated as non‑aligned.

- Physical climate risk assessment: For financed retail properties inside and outside the EU, RBI used an external provider to conduct an acute and chronic physical risk and vulnerability assessment under IPCC RCP 8.5, aligned with Annex I, Appendix A of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139. Assets with very high unmitigated risk did not pass.

- Defining the CSRD client base: Clients were identified using internal data with criteria including EU registration; size thresholds (≥€25m assets or ≥€50m revenue; premiums for insurers; gross operating result for other FIs), updated per Delegated Directive (EU) 2023/2775; capital market orientation/credit institution/insurance undertaking; and >500 employees. Fully consolidated subsidiaries of CSRD clients lacking stand‑alone KPIs were included.

- Data sourcing: Disclosures of taxonomy eligibility/alignment rely on actual information from financial and non‑financial undertakings collected by RBI and supplemented with third‑party data providers.

- GAR (flow): Calculated consistently with GAR (stock) but limited to positions newly concluded in the 2024 financial year.

- Off‑balance sheet exposure: RBI assessed taxonomy alignment for financial guarantees and assets under management. For guarantees, the loans/bonds methodology was applied to underlying transactions; if purpose was unknown, counterparties’ KPIs were used. For AUM, the KPI followed the asset manager approach, using weighted averages of investee taxonomy KPIs. Data was sourced internally and via external providers.

- Continuous improvement: RBI is enhancing processes and ESG data quality and availability through ongoing stakeholder dialogue.
text:
RBI’s assets with exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities at year-end 2024 amounted to €  1,072  million and are 
used in the calculation of the GAR (CapEx). In accordance with the instructions set out in Annex V of the Disclosures Delegated 
Act, the exposures to be included in the numerator encompass banking book loans and advances to CSRD-relevant clients, 
households (limited to loans collateralized by residential real estate), and loans and advances to local governments.
All retail exposures relevant to the EU Taxonomy were analyzed under the relevant economic activities and environmental 
objectives in accordance with the Disclosures Delegated Act and included in the CapEx as well as in the turnover GAR. With 
regard to compliance with minimum social safeguards (MS), the interpretation of the Platform on Sustainable Finance as set 
out in the Final Report on Minimum Safeguards (available at sustainable-finance-platform-finance-report ) was followed, which 
does not cover the application of the MS criteria for retail exposures. The total amount of taxonomy-aligned economic 
activities in the retail sector amounted to €  41 million out of a total of € 1,072  million. The GAR (CapEx) amounted to 0.81 per 
cent, of which 0.03 percentage points corresponded to the contribution of taxonomy-aligned economic activities in the retail 
sector.
RBI has analyzed retail exposures in detail, particularly house purchase loans. Besides identifying thresholds for Nearly Zero 
Energy Buildings (NZEB), analyses identifying the top 15 per cent of the national building stock in terms of Primary Energy 
Demand for economic activity 7.7 (acquisition and ownership of buildings) were included in the calculation, providing these 
analyses were based on transparent real data in line with the relevant frequently asked questions (FAQs) of the EU 
Commission. Estimates, for example based on the year of construction, were only included in the voluntary disclosure. As in the 
previous disclosure for 2023, it was not possible to collect the necessary information from retail customers regarding building 
renovation loans as well as car loans given the detailed and high demands. Such financing was therefore generally recognized 
as taxonomy non-aligned. Group management report                                                                                                                                                    133
 ·  Raiffeisen Bank International | Member of RBI Group | Financial Year 2024   The physical risk assessment for the retail segment was performed with the help of an external provider. A physical risk 
assessment, including a vulnerability analysis, was conducted for the relevant financed properties both within and outside the 
EU in accordance with Appendix A of Annex I of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 of 4 June 2021 supplementing 
Regulation (EU) 2020/852 of the European Parliament and of the Council by establishing the technical screening criteria for 
determining the conditions under which an economic activity qualifies as contributing substantially to climate change 
mitigation or climate change adaptation, and for determining whether that economic activity causes no significant harm to 
any of the other environmental objectives. The physical risk assessment considered acute and chronic risks for the relevant 
hazards as set out in that Appendix and used an Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) RCP 8.5 scenario. The 
assessment was not passed if the seriousness of a threat was considered very high and no corresponding risk mitigation 
measures were taken. 
By referencing internally available data, RBI’s CSRD client base was determined according to the following criteria:
· The country in which the counterparty is registered must be an EU member state.
· The business partner’s total assets (on a consolidated basis) must be equal to or greater than € 25 million or its total  
revenue (turnover) must be equal to or greater than € 50 million. For insurance and reinsurance undertakings, the 
gross premiums written were used instead of revenue, while the gross operating result was used for the other 
financial institutions.
The relevant thresholds as set out in Directive 2013/34/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 
2013 on the annual financial statements, consolidated financial statements and related reports of certain types of 
undertakings amending Directive 2006/43/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Council 
Directives 78/660/EEC and 83/349/EEC (the Accounting Directive) were updated by the Commission Delegated 
Directive (EU) 2023/2775 of 17 October 2023 amending Directive 2013/34/EU of the European Parliament and of the 
Council as regards the adjustments of the size criteria for micro, small, medium-sized and large undertakings or 
groups.
· The customer was either a capital market-oriented company, a credit institution or an insurance undertaking.
· The customer had more than 500 employees on average (on a consolidated basis).
RBI also considered subsidiaries that were fully consolidated under CSRD customers and did not publish/provide taxonomy KPIs 
on a stand-alone basis in a sustainability report.
The disclosure of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned exposures must be based on actual information provided by the 
financial or non-ﬁnancial undertaking. RBI collected such data as part of the data collection project. In addition, third-party 
data providers were used to obtain information for the assessment of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned economic 
activities.

title: Exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (GAR (flow)) (template 4)
heading: Exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (GAR (ﬂow)) (template 4)
start_phrase: The GAR KPI ﬂow was calculated in line with the GAR KPI stock.
summary:
- Conducted a physical climate risk assessment for retail-segment financed properties using an external provider, following Appendix A of Annex I of EU Delegated Regulation 2021/2139, considering acute and chronic hazards under IPCC RCP 8.5; assessments failed where very high threats lacked mitigation measures.
- Defined the CSRD client base using internal data with criteria: EU registration; size thresholds (≥€25m total assets or ≥€50m revenue, with gross premiums written for insurers and gross operating result for other financial institutions); status as capital market-oriented, credit institution, or insurance undertaking; and >500 employees; included fully consolidated subsidiaries lacking standalone taxonomy KPIs.
- Noted updated size thresholds per Commission Delegated Directive (EU) 2023/2775 amending the Accounting Directive (2013/34/EU).
- Stated that disclosure of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned exposures relies on actual counterparty information, collected via an internal data project and supplemented by third-party data providers.
- Described GAR KPI flow (template 4) as aligned with GAR KPI stock methodology but limited to positions newly concluded in the 2024 financial year.
- Assessed off-balance sheet exposures (template 5) for taxonomy alignment with climate change mitigation and adaptation objectives and eligibility for the four additional environmental objectives, separating financial guarantees from assets under management.
- For financial guarantees, applied the loans/bonds methodology to underlying transactions; used counterparties’ KPIs when purposes were unknown; sourced data internally and from external providers.
- For assets under management, calculated the KPI per asset manager methodology using the weighted average of investments in taxonomy-aligned activities, based on counterparties’ taxonomy KPIs; data gathered internally and via external providers.
- Committed to ongoing improvements in ESG data availability, quality, and processes through engagement with stakeholders.

title: Off-balance sheet exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (template 5)
heading: Off-balance sheet exposures to taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets (template 5)
start_phrase: RBI analyzed its off-balance sheet exposure, both with known purposes and general purposes with regard to taxonomy alignment for the ﬁrst two environmental objectives – climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation – and the taxonomy eligibility of the four new environmental objectives.
summary:
- External provider conducted a physical climate risk assessment for retail-segment financed properties inside and outside the EU, following Appendix A of Annex I of EU Delegated Regulation 2021/2139, using the IPCC RCP 8.5 scenario and covering acute and chronic hazards; assessments failed where threats were very high and no mitigation was in place.
- RBI defined its CSRD client base via internal data using criteria: EU registration; size thresholds (assets ≥ €25m or revenue ≥ €50m; insurers by gross premiums; other financial institutions by gross operating result), updated per Delegated Directive 2023/2775; status as capital market-oriented company, credit institution or insurer; and more than 500 employees; fully consolidated subsidiaries without standalone taxonomy KPIs were included.
- Disclosure of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned exposures is based on actual information from clients, supported by RBI’s data collection project and third-party data providers.
- GAR KPI flow (template 4) was calculated consistently with the GAR stock KPI but limited to new positions concluded in the 2024 financial year.
- Off-balance sheet exposures (template 5) were analyzed for taxonomy alignment on climate change mitigation and adaptation and for eligibility under the four new environmental objectives, distinguishing between financial guarantees and assets under management.
- For financial guarantees, the KPI methodology mirrored that for loans, advances, and bonds and was applied to the underlying transaction; where purpose data was missing, counterparties’ KPIs were used; data combined internal collection with external sources.
- For assets under management, the KPI followed the asset manager methodology, using the weighted average value invested in taxonomy-aligned activities and counterparties’ taxonomy KPIs; data was sourced internally and supplemented externally.
- RBI commits to continuous process improvement and enhancing ESG data availability and quality through stakeholder dialogue.
text:
RBI analyzed its off-balance sheet exposure, both with known purposes and general purposes with regard to taxonomy 
alignment for the ﬁrst two environmental objectives – climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation – and the 
taxonomy eligibility of the four new environmental objectives. For the disclosure of off-balance sheet exposures, a distinction 
was made between ﬁnancial guarantees and assets under management.
The methodology for calculating the KPI for ﬁnancial guarantees corresponded to the methodology established for loans and 
advances, as well as for bonds. However, it was applied to the underlying transaction of the ﬁnancial guarantees. If RBI had no 
data on the specific purpose of the underlying transaction, the counterparties‘ KPIs were used. For the earmarked exposures, 
the counterparties‘ taxonomy data was collected internally as part of the data collection project and supplemented by an 
external data provider.
The KPI for assets under management was calculated in line with the methodology determined for asset managers. The 
numerator comprised the weighted average value of the investments in the taxonomy-aligned economic activities of the 
enterprises in which investments were made. Reference was made to the information on the taxonomy eligibility and 
taxonomy alignment of the respective counterparties (financial and non-ﬁnancial CSRD undertakings) and the corresponding 
KPIs were used. For the earmarked exposures, data was also collected internally as part of the data collection project and 
supplemented by an external data provider. RBI is committed to continuously improving its own processes and addressing the 
topic of ESG data availability and quality as part of a constructive dialog with the relevant stakeholders.

title: Exposures to taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets for nuclear and gas economic activities (templates in accordance with Annex XII of the Disclosures Delegated Act)
heading:
Exposures to taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets for 
nuclear and gas economic activities (templates in accordance with Annex XII of the Disclosures 
Delegated Act)
start_phrase: The EU Taxonomy includes six economic activities in the nuclear and gas sector.
summary:
- Focus: Disclosure of exposures to EU Taxonomy-eligible and -aligned activities/assets in the nuclear and gas sectors, following Annex XII of the Disclosures Delegated Act and Article 8 reporting requirements.

- RBI sector policies: A restrictive nuclear policy under the ESG framework and Code of Conduct limits involvement with NPPs, nuclear fuel, and nuclear waste companies; cooperation with electricity companies is allowed only with strict segregation from nuclear-related financing. A sector-specific group policy governs oil and gas activities.

- 2024 exposures and data: No taxonomy-eligible or -aligned exposures earmarked in the gas sector; reliance on companies’ published taxonomy KPIs for both nuclear and gas. KPI collection combined internal efforts with an external provider, covering revenue- and investment-based metrics. For the first time, KPIs of financial undertakings, including other credit institutions, were included.

- Methodological notes: The evolving interpretation of the EU Taxonomy and European Commission FAQs informed 2024 disclosures without exceeding or contradicting Regulation (EU) 2021/2178. Any changes versus the prior year’s presentation are to be detailed in accompanying templates.

- Evolution over time:
  - Non-financial undertakings: Taxonomy-aligned CapEx exposures rose from €716 million to €1,020 million.
  - Financial undertakings: Inclusion had limited impact due to low reported alignment among credit institutions.
  - Retail mortgages: Despite more EPC collection, a change in the climate risk/vulnerability assessment provider reduced aligned volumes from €159 million to €41 million.

- GAR dynamics:
  - Total GAR assets increased from €126 billion to €133 billion.
  - Assets excluded from the numerator but included in the denominator rose from €86 billion to €95 billion.
  - Lower exposure to non-EU counterparties not under CSRD; higher exposure to SMEs.
  - “Other categories of assets” grew from €3 billion to €18 billion due to inclusion of household assets not counted in the numerator and previously outside the GAR scope.
  - Net effect: Higher denominator-only assets negatively impacted RBI’s GAR.
text:
Exposures to taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned economic activities/covered assets for 
nuclear and gas economic activities (templates in accordance with Annex XII of the Disclosures 
Delegated Act)
The EU Taxonomy includes six economic activities in the nuclear and gas sector. Companies operating in these sectors that are 
subject to taxonomy disclosures are therefore required to publish EU Taxonomy data on taxonomy eligibility and taxonomy 
alignment for their relevant nuclear and gas activities.
RBI’s sustainability concept for the nuclear and gas sector is detailed in the ESG framework (business policy on nuclear energy 
and business policy on oil & gas). RBI takes a restrictive approach towards the nuclear sector in accordance with its Code of 
Conduct. RBI implemented this restrictive approach for the following entities and their relevant suppliers in particular: nuclear 
power plants (NPPs), companies mining, processing and trading with nuclear fuel, or companies managing nuclear waste 
(storage of spent fuel derived from NPPs). The above-mentioned policy takes into consideration that NPPs are usually operated 
by electricity companies or holdings. As a consequence thereof, RBI seeks to continue its cooperation with these electricity 
companies or holdings, albeit with strict segregation from nuclear power plants and connected activities (i.e. any financing to 
electricity providers that process energy from nuclear sources is only allowed if the purpose of the financing is not for or 
related to nuclear power plants).
Accordingly, any resultant exposure only stemmed from taxonomy KPIs for the nuclear sector as published by the respective 
companies. In addition, RBI has implemented a sector-speciﬁc group policy for the gas sector, in which it addresses the 
handling of oil and gas economic activities. 
In 2024, RBI had no taxonomy-eligible or taxonomy-aligned exposures earmarked in the gas sector. Accordingly, only the 
taxonomy KPIs published by the companies were used for the gas sector. KPIs for the nuclear and gas sectors were collected 
internally as part of the data collection project and supplemented by an external data provider. For the specific nuclear and 
gas activities of the relevant counterparties, all revenue-based and investment-based taxonomy KPIs were included regarding 
their taxonomy eligibility and taxonomy alignment. For 2024, this also involved the respective KPIs of financial undertakings, 
including other credit institutions for the first time.

title: III. Adjustments in the presentation of information compared to the previous annual reporting period
heading:
III. Adjustments in the presentation of information compared to the previous annual 
reporting period
start_phrase: The EU Taxonomy is a novel framework, and the interpretation of its requirements is still subject to change.
summary:
- Scope: Disclosures of taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned exposures for nuclear and gas activities per Annex XII of the EU Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act.
- Regulatory context: Six nuclear and gas economic activities are covered by the EU Taxonomy; in-scope companies must disclose eligibility and alignment for these activities.
- RBI policies:
  - Nuclear: Restrictive approach per ESG framework and Code of Conduct; applies to NPPs, nuclear fuel mining/processing/trading, and nuclear waste management. Cooperation with electricity companies/holdings is permitted only with strict segregation from nuclear-related financing.
  - Gas: Sector-specific group policy for oil and gas activities.
- 2024 exposure and data approach:
  - No taxonomy-eligible or taxonomy-aligned exposures earmarked in the gas sector; reliance on companies’ published taxonomy KPIs.
  - KPI collection combined internal efforts and an external provider; included revenue- and investment-based KPIs and, for the first time, KPIs of financial undertakings (e.g., credit institutions).
- Presentation changes vs prior year:
  - Evolving interpretation of EU Taxonomy; 2024 disclosures reflect RBI’s current understanding.
  - European Commission FAQs considered where consistent with the Taxonomy Regulation and Delegated Regulation 2021/2178; any interpretation-driven changes are detailed in the templates.
- Evolution over time (2023 to 2024):
  - Increased KPI collection coverage, including financial undertakings.
  - Non-financial undertakings: taxonomy-aligned CapEx exposures rose from €716m to €1,020m.
  - Financial undertakings: limited impact due to low reported alignment among credit institutions.
  - Retail mortgages: despite more EPCs, a change in climate risk/vulnerability data provider reduced aligned loans from €159m to €41m.
  - GAR dynamics: total GAR assets rose from €126bn to €133bn; assets excluded from the numerator but included in the denominator increased from €86bn to €95bn.
  - Portfolio shifts: reduced exposure to non-EU counterparties not under CSRD; increased exposure to SMEs.
  - Other asset categories grew from €3bn to €18bn due to inclusion of certain household assets in the denominator only, which negatively impacted the GAR.
text:
III. Adjustments in the presentation of information compared to the previous annual 
reporting period
The EU Taxonomy is a novel framework, and the interpretation of its requirements is still subject to change. Further guidance, 
such as that provided by the European Commission in the FAQs, can provide clarity and has been continuously monitored and 
evaluated by RBI. The disclosure in accordance with Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy for 2024 reflected RBI’s current understanding 
of the EU Taxonomy. The FAQs of the European Commission were taken into account, insofar as the guidance does not exceed 
the requirements of the Taxonomy Regulation and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 or contradict the 
requirements of those regulations or explanations provided in previous FAQs. Where this interpretation had changed compared 
to the previous annual reporting period and resulted in adjustments in the presentation of information in the disclosure, these 
changes will be described in detail with the respective templates below.

title: IV. Evolution of taxonomy-aligned economic activities over time
heading: IV. Evolution of taxonomy-aligned economic activities over time
start_phrase: For the 2024 financial year, efforts to collect counterparties' taxonomy KPIs increased, and also included KPIs of financial undertakings.
summary:
- Scope: Disclosure of exposures to taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned activities in the nuclear and gas sectors, using templates per Annex XII of the Disclosures Delegated Act, in line with EU Taxonomy Article 8.
- RBI sector policies: Restrictive stance on nuclear activities (NPPs, nuclear fuel supply chain, nuclear waste management) per ESG framework and Code of Conduct; cooperation with electricity companies permitted only with strict segregation from nuclear-related financing. Sector-specific policy for oil & gas. In 2024, no taxonomy-eligible or taxonomy-aligned exposures were earmarked in the gas sector.
- Data approach: Nuclear and gas KPIs (eligibility and alignment) were sourced from company disclosures, collected internally and via an external provider; both revenue- and investment-based KPIs were used. In 2024, KPIs of financial undertakings, including credit institutions, were incorporated for the first time.
- Interpretation updates: Given the evolving EU Taxonomy and European Commission FAQs, 2024 disclosures reflect RBI’s current interpretation, applying FAQs where consistent with Regulation (EU) 2021/2178; any changes versus the prior year will be detailed in the templates.
- Evolution of alignment:
  - Increased counterparty KPI collection, including financial undertakings.
  - Taxonomy-aligned CapEx for non-financial undertakings rose from €716m to €1,020m.
  - Limited contribution from financial undertakings due to low reported alignment.
  - Taxonomy-aligned retail mortgage loans fell from €159m to €41m, driven by a provider change leading to more sensitive climate risk/vulnerability assessments, despite greater EPC collection.
- GAR dynamics:
  - Total GAR assets increased from €126bn to €133bn.
  - Assets excluded from the GAR numerator but included in the denominator rose from €86bn to €95bn.
  - Reduced exposure to non-EU counterparties not subject to CSRD; increased exposure to SMEs.
  - “Other categories of assets” jumped from €3bn to €18bn due to inclusion of certain household assets not counted in the numerator and previously outside the GAR calculation.
  - Overall effect: a larger share of denominator-only assets negatively impacted RBI’s GAR.
text:
IV. Evolution of taxonomy-aligned economic activities over time
For the 2024 financial year, efforts to collect counterparties' taxonomy KPIs increased, and also included KPIs of financial 
undertakings. Taxonomy aligned exposures for non-financial undertakings in terms of CapEx increased from € 716 million to € 
1,020  million. The impact of the inclusion of taxonomy KPIs for financial undertakings was limited as credit institutions in 
particular reported low degrees of taxonomy alignment.
Regarding retail mortgage loans to households, efforts to collect Energy Performance Certificates increased. However, a 
change of provider used for the climate risk and vulnerability assessment resulted in a lower number of retail mortgage loans 
to be determined as taxonomy-aligned due the higher sensitivity of the data. Overall, taxonomy-aligned retail mortgage loans 
decreased from € 159 million to € 41 million.
From 2023 to 2024, the share of assets excluded from the numerator of the GAR but covered in the denominator increased. 
While total GAR assets increased from € 126 billion to € 133 billion, assets excluded from the numerator of the GAR but covered 
in the denominator increased from € 86 billion to € 95 billion. The exposure to non-EU counterparties that were not subject to 
the CSRD was reduced. However, exposure to SMEs increased for the 2024 financial year. In addition, the position of other 
categories of assets increased significantly from € 3 billion to € 18 billion due to the inclusion of household assets that were 
not considered in the numerator of the GAR and were previously included in the assets not covered in the GAR calculation. 
Overall, the increase in assets that were only covered in the denominator negatively affected RBI's GAR.Group management report                                                                                                                                                    135

title: Disclosure template 1 – assets for the calculation of GAR
heading: Disclosure template 1 – assets for the calculation of GAR
start_phrase:
1. This template shall include information for loans and advances, debt securities and equity instruments in the banking book, towards financial corporates, non-
financial corporates (NFC), including SMEs, households (including residential real estate, house renovation loans and motor vehicle loans only) and local governments/

summary:
- Purpose and scope: Disclosure Template 1 for the Green Asset Ratio (GAR) under the EU Taxonomy, detailing banking book assets (loans and advances, debt securities, equity instruments) toward financial corporates, non-financial corporates (incl. SMEs), households (residential mortgages, renovation, motor vehicle loans), and local governments (housing). It covers accounting categories at amortised cost, FVOCI, designated/mandatorily FVTPL, investments in subsidiaries/joint ventures/associates, and real estate collateral obtained through possession.

- Methodological notes:
  - Non‑EU exposures: Banks with non‑EU subsidiaries disclose a separate GAR for non‑EU counterparties on a best‑effort basis (estimates/proxies with stated assumptions and limitations).
  - Motor vehicle loans: include only exposures originated after the disclosure application date.
  - FY2024 clarifications: repossessed collateral (row 31) excluded from row 1; household assets not relevant for GAR are shown in “other categories of assets” (row 47) rather than “assets not covered” (row 49), since they remain in GAR KPI numerator/denominator per Article 7(1) of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178.

- Structure of disclosure:
  - GAR assets split between numerator and denominator, with a separate block for assets excluded from the numerator but included in the denominator (e.g., SMEs/NFCs not subject to NFRD, non‑EU counterparties, derivatives, interbank on‑demand loans, cash, other assets).
  - Assets not covered for GAR calculation listed separately (central governments/supranationals, central banks, trading book).
  - Breakdowns by counterparty type (credit institutions, other financial corporations, insurance undertakings), by product (loans, debt securities incl. use‑of‑proceeds, equity), and by retail sub‑types (residential mortgages, renovation loans, motor vehicle loans).
  - Environmental objectives covered: Climate Change Mitigation (CCM), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Water and Marine Resources (WTR), Circular Economy (CE), Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC), Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO).
  - Additional categorisations: taxonomy‑eligible vs taxonomy‑aligned, and of which “use of proceeds,” “transitional,” and “enabling” activities.
  - Off‑balance sheet: disclosure of financial guarantees (with taxonomy eligibility/alignment) and assets under management.

- Key FY2024 results (CapEx KPI basis, Group, €m):
  - Total assets: 200,725; Total GAR assets: 132,548.
  - CCM: taxonomy‑eligible 29,338; taxonomy‑aligned 1,063; including UoP 41, transitional 224, enabling 415.
  - Other objectives (small volumes): CCA ~51 eligible; CE ~15 eligible; WTR/PPC/BIO negligible; combined TOTAL across objectives: eligible ~29,404; aligned ~1,072; UoP 41; transitional 224; enabling 415.

Disclosure template 1 – assets for the calculation of GAR
1. This template shall include information for loans and advances, debt securities and equity instruments in the banking book, towards financial corporates, non-
financial corporates (NFC), including SMEs, households (including residential real estate, house renovation loans and motor vehicle loans only) and local governments/
municipalities (house financing). 
2. The following accounting categories of financial assets should be considered: Financial assets at amortised cost, financial assets at fair value through other 
comprehensive income, investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates, financial assets designated at fair value through profit or loss and non-trading 
financial assets mandatorily at fair value through profit or loss, and real estate collaterals obtained by credit institutions by taking possession in exchange in of 
cancellation of debts.
3. Banks with non-EU subsidiary should provide this information separately for exposures towards non-EU counterparties. For non-EU exposures, while there are 
additional challenges in terms of absence of common disclosure requirements and methodology, as the EU taxonomy and the NFRD apply only at EU level, given the 
relevance of these exposures for those credit institutions with non-EU subsidiaries, these institutions should disclose a separate GAR for non-EU exposures, on a best 
effort basis, in the form of estimates and ranges, using proxies, and explaining the assumptions, caveats and limitations.
4. For motor vehicle loans, institutions shall only include those exposures generated after the date of application of the disclosure.
For the financial year 2024, collateral obtained by taking possession as set out in row 31 is not included in row 1 (which includes 
loans and advances, debt securities and equity instruments).
For the financial year 2024, assets related to household exposures which are not relevant for the GAR calculation (i.e. exposures 
not included in the green asset ratio for retail exposures as set out in section 1.2.1.3. of Annex V of the Commission Delegated 
Regulation (EU) 2021/2178) are included in row 47 (other categories of assets) and not in row 49 (assets not covered for GAR 
calculation), as these exposures are not excluded from the calculation of the numerator and denominator of the key 
performance indicators in accordance with Article 7(1) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178.

heading: Template 2 – GAR sector information
start_phrase:
1. Credit institutions shall disclose in this template information on exposures in the banking book towards those sectors covered by the Taxonomy (NACE sectors 4 
levels of detail), using the relevant NACE Codes on the basis of the principal activity of the counterparty.
summary: This section defines Template 2 – GAR sector information and presents Raiffeisen Bank International’s banking-book exposures by NACE 4‑digit sectors in line with the EU Taxonomy, with allocation based solely on the immediate counterparty’s principal activity and, for jointly incurred exposures, on the obligor most relevant to granting the exposure. It discloses, as of 31/12/2024, gross carrying amounts (in € million) and “of which environmentally sustainable” amounts split between non‑financial corporates subject to NFRD and SMEs/other NFCs, across Taxonomy objectives: Climate Change Mitigation (CCM), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Water and marine resources (WTR), Circular economy (CE), Pollution (PPC), and Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO). Under CCM for NFRD corporates, notable gross/sustainable amounts include Activities of head offices (7010) 513/345, Production of electricity (3511) 161/156, Manufacture of motor vehicles (2910) 155/43, Wholesale of grain etc. (4621) 125/114, Transport via pipeline (4950) 103/102, Distribution of gaseous fuels (3522) 89/66, Trade of electricity (3514) 32/31, Basic iron and steel (2410) 77/23, and Trade of gas (3523) 37/37; some sectors (e.g., Loaded electronic boards (2612) 204/0) show non‑sustainable exposures. For SMEs under CCM, amounts are limited (e.g., Fertilisers (2015) 9/9; Computers wholesale (4651) 5/0). For CCA, PPC, and BIO, values are reported as nil across sectors, while WTR and CE show only small gross amounts with no sustainable portion indicated (e.g., WTR: Electronic components (2611) 1, Construction of buildings (4120) 1, Computers wholesale (4651) 6; CE: Wired telecommunications (6110) 3, Activities of head offices (7010) 4).
text:
Template 2 – GAR sector information
1. Credit institutions shall disclose in this template information on exposures in the banking book towards those sectors covered by the Taxonomy (NACE sectors 4 
levels of detail), using the relevant NACE Codes on the basis of the principal activity of the counterparty.
2. The counterparty NACE sector allocation shall be based exclusively on the nature of the immediate counterparty. The classification of the exposures incurred jointly 
by more than one obligor shall be done on the basis of the characteristics of the obligor that was the more relevant, or determinant, for the institution to grant the 
exposure. The distribution of jointly incurred exposures by NACE codes shall be driven by the characteristics of the more relevant or determinant obligor. Institutions 
shall disclose information by NACE codes with the level of disaggregation required in the template.

- Tables present sector codes, labels, and amounts for each counterparty group, indicating where activities are taxonomy-eligible and environmentally sustainable.
- Includes page references and footnote markers (e.g., u, v, w, x, y, z, aa, ab) indicating additional notes not shown in the excerpt.

  - Many other sectors display limited or no environmentally sustainable amounts (indicated by dashes).

summary:
- The excerpt presents EU Taxonomy disclosures from Raiffeisen Bank International’s 2024 Group management report, showing Green Asset Ratio (GAR) sector information based on turnover.
- Data are broken down by NACE Rev.2 4‑digit sectors and segmented by client type: non‑financial corporates subject to NFRD versus SMEs and other non‑financial corporates not subject to NFRD.
- For 31/12/2023, it reports totals across environmental objectives combined (CCM, CCA, WTR, CE, PPC, BIO), providing gross carrying amounts and the portion that is environmentally sustainable for each sector.
- For 31/12/2024, it separately reports:
  - Climate Change Mitigation (CCM): gross carrying amounts and taxonomy‑aligned portions by sector.
  - Climate Change Adaptation (CCA): a sectoral table that, in this extract, shows no reported amounts.
- Sectors covered span extraction, manufacturing (e.g., iron and steel, electronics, motor vehicles, rolling stock), energy (production, distribution, and trade of electricity and gas), construction, wholesale/retail, transportation and logistics (rail, air support, other transport support), postal/courier services, accommodation, ICT and information services, real estate (renting/management), head offices and management consulting, technical testing and R&D, public administration support, and health/social care.
- The CCM 2024 table highlights notable reported exposures and taxonomy‑aligned amounts in areas such as head office activities, production and trade of electricity, certain manufacturing (e.g., loaded electronic boards, motor vehicles), wholesale of metals and construction materials, freight rail transport, and gas distribution.
- Footnote markers (e.g., a–d, e–h) appear, indicating methodological notes or clarifications that are not included in this partial extract.
- Page references indicate this content spans pages 188–190 of the Group management report.

start_phrase: Breakdown by sector -
summary:
The extract presents Raiffeisen Bank International’s EU Taxonomy disclosures for 31/12/2024 within the Group management report (FY 2024, pp. 190–191). It shows a sectoral breakdown at NACE Rev. 2 4‑digit level of the bank’s exposures to non‑financial corporates, split between entities subject to the NFRD and SMEs/other NFCs not subject to the NFRD. For each sector, the tables report gross carrying amounts (in € million) and the portion classified as environmentally sustainable for the Taxonomy environmental objective Climate Change Adaptation (CCA); a subsequent section introduces the same breakdown for Water and marine resources (WTR).

The coverage spans a wide range of activities across extraction, manufacturing (chemicals, metals, electronics, machinery, vehicles), utilities (electricity and gas), waste, construction, wholesale/retail trade, transport and logistics, ICT and telecoms, real estate, professional and technical services, public administration-related activities, health/social care, and recreation. The CCA table indicates that most sectors show no (or de minimis) Taxonomy‑aligned amounts, with a minor reported exposure in “Other amusement and recreation activities.” The WTR section header appears, signalling an analogous sectoral disclosure for that objective, though detailed figures are not included in the excerpt.

summary:
Partial extract from Raiffeisen Bank International’s 2024 Group Management Report showing EU Taxonomy disclosures as of 31/12/2023. It presents sectoral breakdowns by NACE 4‑digit codes of the bank’s exposures to non-financial corporates, split between entities subject to the NFRD and SMEs/other NFCs not subject to the NFRD. For each sector, the tables display gross carrying amounts in € million and the share classified as environmentally sustainable under three environmental objectives: Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Water and Marine Resources (WTR), and Circular Economy (CE).

The listings span a wide range of industries (extraction, manufacturing, energy generation/transmission/distribution, construction, wholesale/retail, transport and storage, postal/courier, accommodation, software/telecom/IT, real estate, head offices/consultancy, testing/R&D, leasing, facility support, public administration, care, and recreation). Most sectors show no reported amounts (indicated by dashes). A notable exception is NACE 6820 (Renting and operating of own or leased real estate), which shows reported figures of 109 and 51 (in € million) in the CCA table. The content is paginated across the report (pages ~200–202) and references footnotes not included in the excerpt.

summary:
Extract from Raiffeisen Bank International’s Group Management Report (FY2024) presenting EU Taxonomy-related disclosures as of 31/12/2023. It shows a sectoral breakdown at NACE 4-digit level for two environmental objectives—Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC) and Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO)—with bank exposures reported as gross carrying amounts (in € million) and the portion deemed environmentally sustainable. Figures are split between Non-Financial Corporates subject to the NFRD and SMEs/other NFCs not subject to the NFRD.

The document lists a wide range of sectors across manufacturing, energy and utilities, construction, wholesale/retail trade, transportation and logistics, postal and courier services, hospitality, ICT/telecoms, real estate, head offices/consultancy, testing/R&D, facilities support, public administration, and social care. Many lines show no amounts (“—”), while the BIO section includes concrete amounts and sustainable portions for selected sectors, such as:
- Manufacture of basic iron and steel (104 total; 44 sustainable); motor vehicles (186; 15); plastics/rubber machinery (19; 3); electricity production (44; 38); electricity trade (8; 6); gas distribution (52; 10); gas trade (13; 13); wholesale of metals (32; 14); wholesale of wood/construction materials (49; 49); passenger rail transport (189; —); inland freight water transport (10; —); other transport support (5; 2); postal/courier activities (small amounts with some sustainable portions); wholesale of grain/tobacco/seeds/feeds (23; 11).

The excerpt ends with a heading indicating a forthcoming total across all six environmental objectives (CCM, CCA, WTR, CE, PPC, BIO), implying consolidated sectoral totals follow beyond the provided text. Overall, the section’s purpose is to disclose the bank’s taxonomy-relevant exposures and the share classified as environmentally sustainable, by sector and by counterparty regulatory scope.

- Gross carrying amount (in € million)
- The portion classified as environmentally sustainable under the EU Taxonomy objectives (CCM, CCA, WTR, CE, PPC, BIO)

The table splits exposures between non-financial corporates subject to the NFRD and SMEs/other NFCs not subject to the NFRD. It spans extraction, manufacturing (e.g., sugar, cement, basic iron and steel, motor vehicles, plastics machinery, electronic components), energy (electricity production, distribution and trade; gas distribution and trade), wholesale/retail (e.g., wood and construction materials, metals, grain/feeds, cars/parts), transport and logistics (passenger rail, inland water freight, transport support, postal/courier), real estate (renting/operating), head offices/holding companies, and selected services (telecoms, IT).

Notable larger exposures and/or higher taxonomy-aligned amounts appear in:
- Manufacture of motor vehicles
- Basic iron and steel
- Production and trade of electricity
- Distribution and trade of gas
- Wholesale of wood/construction materials (fully aligned in the excerpt)
- Wholesale of metals and of grain/feeds
- Passenger rail transport and inland water freight
- Renting and operating of real estate
- Activities of head offices

Many other sectors show no or minimal taxonomy-aligned amounts. The excerpt is from the Group management report (FY 2024), pages 206–207.

title: Template 3 – GAR KPI stock - Introduction
heading: Template 3 – GAR KPI stock
start_phrase: 1. Institution shall dislcose in this template the GAR KPIs on stock of loans calculated based on the data disclosed in template 1, on covered assets, and by applying the formulas proposed in this template
summary: Introduces Template 3 for disclosing Green Asset Ratio (GAR) KPIs on the stock of loans, calculated from Template 1 data on covered assets using the prescribed formulas, and requiring disclosure of the proportion of total assets covered by the GAR. Institutions may additionally report the share of assets funding taxonomy-relevant sectors that are environmentally sustainable (taxonomy-aligned) to enrich the KPI. The template must be duplicated for revenue-based and CapEx-based disclosures. For financial year 2024, proportions are calculated by dividing eligible or aligned assets from Template 1 (Assets for the calculation of the GAR) by the respective covered assets (Template 1, column a, rows 1–31 and 48), rather than Total GAR assets (row 48), to align with Annex V Sections 1.2.1.1, 1.2.1.2, 1.2.1.4, and 1.2.1.5 of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178.
text:
Template 3 – GAR KPI stock
1. Institution shall dislcose in this template the GAR KPIs on stock of loans calculated based on the data disclosed in template 1, on covered assets, and by applying the 
formulas proposed in this template
2. Information on the GAR (green asset ratio of 'eligible' activities) shall be accompanied with information on the proportion of total assets covered by the GAR
3. Credit institutions can, in addition to the information included in this template, show the proportion of assets funding taxonomy relevant sectors that are 
environmetnally sustainable (Taxonomy-aligned). This information would enrich the information on the KPI on  environmentatlly sustainable assets compared to total 
covered assets
4. Credit institutions shall duplicate this template for revenue based and CapEx based disclosures
Note: For the financial year 2024, in order to accurately reflect the information to be disclosed in accordance with Sections 
1.2.1.1., 1.2.1.2., 1.2.1.4. and 1.2.1.5. of Annex V of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178, the proportions to be disclosed 
in this template are calculated by dividing the relevant eligible or aligned assets as recorded in template 1 (Assets for the 
calculation of the GAR) by the respective covered assets (as recorded in column a, rows 1-31 and 48 of that template) instead 
of the Total GAR assets (as set out in row 48 of that asset).

- Purpose and scope: Template 3 – GAR KPI stock sets out how credit institutions must disclose the Green Asset Ratio (GAR) key performance indicators on the stock of loans, using covered assets and the formulas in this template, based on data from Template 1.
- Required disclosures:
  - Proportion of total assets covered by the GAR.
  - For taxonomy‑relevant sectors: proportions of covered assets that are Taxonomy‑eligible and Taxonomy‑aligned.

- 2024 methodology note: For FY2024, proportions are calculated by dividing eligible/aligned assets (from Template 1) by covered assets (Template 1, column a, rows 1–31 and 48) rather than by Total GAR assets.
- Coverage and granularity:
  - Instruments not held for trading: loans and advances, debt securities (including Use of Proceeds instruments), and equity instruments.
  - Counterparty sectors: financial undertakings (including credit institutions, other financial corporations, investment firms, management companies, insurance undertakings), non‑financial undertakings, households (with sub‑items for residential real‑estate, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans), local governments (housing and other financing), and collateral obtained.
- Headline results as of 31/12/2024 (CapEx‑based):

  - Climate Change Adaptation (CCA): Total GAR assets show 0.04% Taxonomy‑eligible and 0.01% Taxonomy‑aligned; of which 0.00% Use of Proceeds and 0.00% enabling reported in the table.
- Presentation: Figures are expressed as proportions of total covered assets, with numerator and denominator restricted to GAR‑covered assets. The data is part of Raiffeisen Bank International’s Group management report for financial year 2024.

Figures are shown for Climate Change Mitigation (CCM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), split by counterparty and instrument type, and broken down into taxonomy-eligible vs. taxonomy-aligned, with “of which” for Use of Proceeds, transitional, and enabling activities.
- Portfolio coverage: Focus on loans and advances, debt securities (including Use of Proceeds instruments), and equity instruments not held for trading, across financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financial corporations, investment firms, management companies, insurance undertakings), non-financial undertakings, households (including mortgages, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans), local government financing, and collateral obtained.
- CCM results (headline): Total GAR assets show 21.83% taxonomy-eligible and 0.39% taxonomy-aligned, including 0.03% Use of Proceeds, 0.13% transitional, and 0.18% enabling.
- CCM breakdown highlights:
  - Financial undertakings exhibit very low eligibility and alignment across loans, debt securities, and equities.
  - Non-financial undertakings show notable eligibility and some alignment, with contributions from loans and debt securities; enabling and transitional components are present.
  - Households exhibit very high taxonomy-eligibility (driven largely by mortgages) but minimal alignment; building renovation loans show no reported contribution; motor vehicle loans have limited eligibility.
  - Local government financing and collateral obtained register near-zero contributions.
- CCA results: Essentially no taxonomy-eligible or taxonomy-aligned assets reported across all categories (totals at 0.00%); any category-level non-zero figures are negligible and do not change the total.
- Overall message: The bank’s GAR exposure is concentrated in CCM, with a meaningful eligible share but a low aligned share; CCA exposure is currently negligible.
